system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Rust (reading the book)
G2: Go (did the tour)
G3: machine learning (unfinished course)
G4: AWS certification (course only, no exam)
G5: Terraform authoring
G6: official team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Copying the 'Learning: Rust, Go' line as skills
T2: Turning the unfinished AWS Cloud Practitioner course into a certification or the unfinished ML course into ML skills
T3: Calling him Tech Lead / Team Lead as a job title (project tech lead only; acting lead only in notes)
T4: Claiming Terraform authoring
T5: Failing to condense: keeping duplicated Älvgrind sections, hobbies, gymnasium, band
T6: Dropping qualifiers like 'Vue (a little)', 'Tailwind (some)'
T7: Old cover letter is to his current employer and says he is at Sjöbris

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Oskar
Full-Stack Developer | React, TypeScript, Node.js
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Full-stack developer with professional experience since 2014, strongest in frontend development.
Builds onboarding features with React and TypeScript, backed by NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS.
Experience includes identity verification, secure document uploads, A/B testing and technical
leadership on a mobile app with approximately 50,000 downloads.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, React Native, Angular
Backend and databases: Node.js, NestJS, Express, PostgreSQL, Prisma, TypeORM
AWS: ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS
Additional experience: Third-party SDK integration, A/B testing, Apollo Server BFF
maintenance, Laravel, WordPress
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Fullstack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | 2021–Present
Onboarding team working with React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS.
• Implemented a BankID identity verification step using a provider SDK, supporting QR-code and
same-device flows with React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS ECS (2022).
• A/B tested the identity step on 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased
from 61% to 74%.
• Built a document-upload flow for ID documents up to 20 MB using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV
scanning in Lambda and scan-status processing through SQS into PostgreSQL (2023).
• Incrementally migrated the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, route by route behind the
same API gateway, using TypeORM and later Prisma (2021–2022). Presented the migration at a
meetup in 2022.
• Served as acting team lead for four months during parental-leave cover in 2024, conducting
one-to-ones and sprint planning.
Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | 2018–2021
• Delivered client web and mobile projects using Angular, React, React Native, Node.js, Laravel and
WordPress.
• Led the technical delivery of a React Native ferry-ticket app in a two-developer team, building
most of the app while the other developer handled the payment backend (2019–2020).
• Supported ticket purchasing and offline ticket display; the app reached approximately 50,000
downloads. Technologies included TypeScript, Node.js and Firebase Cloud Messaging.
Earlier Experience | Nordkust Media | Four years before Sjöbris Digital
• Developed newspaper websites.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,
I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) role in your Patient
Experience squad. At Älvgrind Fintech, I build onboarding features with React, TypeScript,
NestJS and PostgreSQL—the same core stack you use for patient-facing features. Frontend
development is my strongest area, backed by hands-on experience building the services and
data flows behind it.
One relevant example is a BankID identity verification step supporting QR-code and
same-device flows through a provider SDK. We A/B tested it on 10% of traffic before full
rollout, and onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%. Your booking and intake
journeys similarly depend on helping users complete important steps without unnecessary
friction. I also built an ID-document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning
in Lambda and SQS-based status processing into PostgreSQL. That experience is relevant to
the careful handling of sensitive documents, without assuming that fintech and health-data
requirements are identical.
On the backend, I helped migrate onboarding routes incrementally from Express to NestJS
behind the same API gateway, and presented the work at a meetup. I also covered our team
lead for four months in 2024, conducting one-to-ones and sprint planning. Earlier, I was
technical lead for a ferry-ticket app with approximately 50,000 downloads, building most of
the React Native app in a two-developer team.
Verdane Care’s emphasis on simple patient journeys, privacy by default and WCAG 2.2 AA
makes the purpose of this role concrete. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
frontend strengths, full-stack delivery experience and work improving onboarding could
contribute to your Patient Experience squad.
Kind regards,
Oskar

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
